content_voiceover: This slide covers the risk stratification section of the TPOG-AML-2021 protocol. Low risk patients receive five courses of chemotherapy and are not eligible for stem cell transplant. Low risk is defined by favorable cytogenetics: inversion 16, t(8;21), NPM1 mutation, or CENPA, combined with MRD less than 0.1 percent after the first induction course. Intermediate risk patients receive six courses of chemotherapy and are also not transplant candidates; this group is essentially defined by exclusion, meaning the absence of any low risk or high risk features. High risk patients are candidates for stem cell transplant, and this category is defined by the presence of any of seven criteria. The first is a long list of specific high risk cytogenetic and molecular lesions, including DEK-NUP214 from t(6;9), KAT6A-CREBBP from t(8;16), monosomy 7, monosomy 5, or 5q deletion, KMT2A-MLLT6 from t(6;11), KMT2A-MLLT10 from t(10;11), inversion 3 at q21q26.2, CBFA2T3-GLIS2 from inversion 16 at p13.3q24.3, NUP98-KDM5A, ETV6-HLXB, NUP98-HOXA9, and NUP98-NSD1. Second is FLT3-ITD combined with either NUP98-NSD1 fusion or WT1 mutation. Third is AML with minimal differentiation or acute erythroid leukemia. Fourth is acute megakaryoblastic leukemia specifically when it carries KMT2A rearrangements, CBFA2T3-GLIS2, or NUP98-KDM5, noting that other megakaryoblastic leukemia subtypes are only intermediate risk. Fifth is treatment related, or secondary, AML. Sixth is refractory anemia with excess blasts and more than 10 percent bone marrow blasts, or AML arising from prior MDS. And seventh is poor response to therapy, defined as MRD 1 percent or higher after induction one, or MRD 0.1 percent or higher after induction two.
keypoints: Low risk: favorable cytogenetics like inv16, t(8;21), NPM1, or CENPA, plus MRD under 0.1 percent after induction I, gets 5 chemo courses only
Intermediate risk is defined by absence of low- or high-risk features, gets 6 chemo courses, no SCT
High risk patients are SCT candidates, defined by any of seven adverse features
High-risk cytogenetics include DEK-NUP214, KAT6A-CREBBP, monosomy 5 or 7, several KMT2A and NUP98 fusions
Poor response also defines high risk: MRD 1 percent or higher after induction I, or 0.1 percent or higher after induction II
keypoint_voiceover: Bottom line for AML risk groups. Low risk means favorable cytogenetics plus a good early MRD response, treated with five courses and no transplant. Intermediate risk is everyone without low- or high-risk features, getting six courses. High risk, which makes patients transplant candidates, includes a long list of adverse cytogenetic and molecular lesions, FLT3-ITD with NUP98-NSD1 or WT1 mutation, minimally differentiated or erythroid AML, certain megakaryoblastic leukemias, secondary AML, and simply a poor MRD response after induction.
